name: Nora
quote: Of Spring's flowers, of Autumn's moon, the winds speak of the eons. The path of the worldly goes on, as if all a theatric dream.

voices.label: Good Morning
voices.text: Is it morning already? I can't believe I wrote all night... (Sigh) If only I could push my deadline back by another two days.

voices.label: Good Afternoon
voices.text:
Want to watch a movie with me?
Work...? It's the afternoon, how can you work in the afternoon?

voices.label: Good Evening
voices.text: Be quiet when you come back at night. I don't want to be disturbed when I watch mo... Ah, I mean, when I'm analyzing scenes. I don't slack off, you know.

voices.label: Good Night
voices.text: It's really quiet late at night in the Oasis. Just looking at the contrast between night and day for various buildings is enough to get my inspiration flowing. In any case, let's just make a note of it first.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 1
voices.text: Artists and writers are fundamentally the same thing. The first procrastinates till the deadline, and so too, does the second.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 2
voices.text: Banknotes are almost gone in this day and age. I was hoping for the chance to print a face onto one.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 3
voices.text:
I'm reading now, so please be quiet.
...Ah, did you want to say something?

voices.label: Home Screen 5
voices.text: ...Hang on, I'll take you there.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 1
voices.text: Don't touch my bangs, it'll interfere with my inspiration.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 2
voices.text: This isn't a family friendly method of hitting on people, you know. Best be careful you don't end up in my next work.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 3
voices.text: Hm? Have I uncovered a hidden trait of yours?

voices.label: On Duty
voices.text: I guess I can't escape the fate of filling shifts even in a place like this.

voices.label: Obtain
voices.text: I'm Nora, though that's a pen name. Idle chatter aside, I'd like a quiet environment... my deadline is approaching and I haven't written a thing yet.

voices.label: Potential Breakthrough
voices.text: I feel inspiration coming on.

voices.label: Neural Expansion
voices.text: I see it... The secret of the words.

voices.label: Max Rank
voices.text: I think I know how to write better prose now.

voices.label: Join Team
voices.text: You want to send a screenwriter onto the battlefield...? Well, because it's you that's asking, or rather, because I have an official excuse to delay my submissions now... alright.

voices.label: Battle Start
voices.text: There is no joy that does not come from suffering.

voices.label: Ultimate Skill
voices.text: The pen is mightier than the sword.

voices.label: MVP 1
voices.text: So, can I knock off now...?

voices.label: MVP 2
voices.text: I've got enough material for my next story.

voices.label: Defeat
voices.text: Owie... I think... I'll have to... delay my manuscript...

voices.label: Oath
voices.text:
I always thought that the things I'd forgotten were very important things. Someone took away my past and replaced it with a void. So I've been writing all this time, not daring to stop, afraid that someday, I'd lose my present, just like before.
Do you still want to be a part of my story, even after knowing this? Do you want to be a part of a scrapbook like myself, with an indistinct cover, a muddled spine, and filled to the brim with abnormality? I'll record your promise, your feelings, and every last bit of you.
Words will always last longer than our actions in the present. Once you're written in, you can never be erased, Professor.

voices.label: New Year
voices.text:
I've never experienced spending the new year with someone else. It's strange, the last person I saw last year was you, and the first person I see this year is also you...
Here's a line I just wrote. What do you think of it?

voices.label: Valentine's Day
voices.text: I've written many love scenes before, and at times like this, giving chocolates out of obligation or genuine affection easily leads to unnecessary developments, so this is all I'm giving you—dried fish and peanuts. Want it?

voices.label: Tanabata
voices.text:
So it's the story of Hikoboshi and Orihime... Is there no continuation to it? What a shame, the source material is so good!
If only I could write their tragedy for a year after their parting and wrap it up with a happy ending on the last day, it would probably be... No, I'm sure it'd be a best-seller novel!

voices.label: Halloween
voices.text: Shhh, don't tell anyone that I'm here. My editor is way scarier than these monsters.

voices.label: Christmas
voices.text: What's the matter, are you surprised to see me dressed up like this? I do celebrate Christmas too, you know. Not out of tradition, of course, but just to collect material.

voices.label: Birthday Wish
voices.text:
This book is for you. It's a doujin novel I wrote after coming to the Oasis, with you as the main character. I wrote all the Dolls in as your harem, including their cats and dogs and ermines and whatever.
What, you don't like it? Why do you have that weird look on your face? When I was outside, everyone paid big bucks for me to write things like that.

voices.label: Neural Cloud
voices.text: Neural Cloud.

voices.label: Intimacy 1
voices.text: Professor, recently I've been thinking about a script starring you, but I found a problem while I was doing character design. Your background and your performance seem very much at odds with each other. Here we have a professor who's been doing research for many years and has a certain degree of fame for it, who goes on to demonstrate extraordinary skill in combat leadership. I can't seem to resolve this contradiction no matter how I try to reconcile your past. Could you explain the reason behind this to me?

voices.label: Intimacy 2
voices.text:
My works? One moment please... That's right, they're all my works.
It's not particularly impressive, it's just that my experiences were different from those of other screenwriter Dolls.
There's a section of my memories which has been erased. While I don't know what exactly was in them, I now have a better understanding of the concept of "loss".

voices.label: Intimacy 3
voices.text:
I sometimes envy my human colleagues. I always get the feeling that the words they write contain a strange thing that I don't understand. It's clearly the same style of writing, but I never get tired of reading it.
I think humans call this divine gift "wit", and one day I'll find out exactly what it is. I'm sure Doll screenwriters will be able to come up with works that transcend established formulas too.

voices.label: Intimacy 4
voices.text:
I like being an author very much, because I can experience a different life through words. It's a very strange feeling—in just a few tens of thousands of words, one can go from nothing to something, ascend from the foothills of mountains to the clouds at its peak, and perfectly live another life.
Still, it's not like it doesn't come at a price. My neural cloud systems have always been more susceptible to overloading than those of other Dolls. I guess it's because I keep experiencing complex emotions. From a religious point of view, one could consider it a form of ascetic study.

voices.label: Intimacy 5
voices.text:
I've written many stories in the past, but no matter what I do, I can't fill up that gap in my life and get rid of the emptiness and fear it brings.
I once thought that I would just have to live on with that emptiness and fear, until one day when my neural cloud system would finally give up that ghost and crash for good.
And then, I met you, like a mentor from all those heroic stories. I wasn't able to make sense of it for a long time, but I learned how to face my present and pen my future.
If I can't change a script's beginning, then I'll just have to make the following scenes and the conclusion more exciting, right?

voices.label: Dissatisfied
voices.text: Hm...

voices.label: Surprised
voices.text: What?

career:
The EW-55 is a special-purpose writer Doll developed by Cyber Media, primarily intended for narrative design and scriptwriting. In order to address the issues with Doll-produced prose, such as dullness and a lack of congruency, the EW-55 is specially equipped with an information processing system possessing a degree of randomness, allowing the EW-55 a chance to generate new ideas from any received information, thus simulating the process of "inspiration" experienced by human writers.

As a popular Doll screenwriter, Nora's works spanned the fields of film, television, literature, games and many others. In order to give her the chance to collect more material for future work, Nora's studio decided to enter her into Project Neural Cloud.
infoStories:
Following the surge in demand for entertainment products, authorial Dolls have seen broad use in many fields as replacements for screenwriters, but scripts produced through theoretical data and language algorithms are invariably dry and stilted. In order to overcome this bottleneck, Cyber Media developed the EW-55, which could experience "inspiration".

Nora's works stem entirely from the chance resonance of various sorts of materials within her neural cloud. She has a chance to convert each piece of new information she receives into a unique idea. In Nora's eyes, the entire world is a database for her to reference, and so she is constantly scribbling notes in an effort to preserve the spark of creativity, and works produced in this way never fail to excite their audience.

However, Nora's productive efficiency is also very vexing. When she lacks for inspiration, she cannot produce anything regardless of the methods used. Conversely, long periods of operation will overload her neural cloud and cause her to crash, regardless of how inspired she is. Trying to get a script out of Nora in a timely manner has always been the thorniest problem her clients have faced.

Nora's rise to fame could be considered an accident. At the time, the EW-55 line faced retirement due to all sorts of negative feedback, and Nora herself was nothing more than a prototype that had been abandoned by Cyber Media. A film studio purchased Nora at a rock-bottom price, but even then, she spent a whole month idle after being switched on. When the studio thought she was defective and wanted to return her, a chance visit to a certain folklorist resulted in her producing a horror movie script in one night, albeit one that did not match the requirements given.

The studio decided to produce the movie with an experimental mindset, and it won much acclaim for its clever plot and creative design, reaping a huge harvest at the box office. The studio immediately allocated their best production crew to Nora and gave her generous time to write, anticipating the next big moneymaker from her.

However, they had to wait nearly half a year for it.

"Didn't you say there was no deadline for the script? I was collecting material all this time," Nora lazily replied to pressing inquiries from her investors as she showed off the scribbles in her notepad, without a single proper sentence in sight.

From then on, Nora was plagued by a new nightmare, known as "deadlines".

In order to encourage the typically slack Nora to collect more information in search of inspiration, the studio actively arranged for her to interact with Dolls from various different fields in the hope that she would collect material from them. Initially, this did little to move Nora, until she saw the name of the folklorist Zangyin on the list of names.

Nora thought that her much-acclaimed debut work would receive praise from Zangyin. Instead, Zangyin proceeded to levy a barrage of ruthless personal attacks against her and her work, pointing out each and every one of the film's errors. Incensed, Nora hit back as well, hinting that everything Zangyin said was nothing more than foolish superstition that nobody would bother with.

The information-gathering meeting soon became an intense dispute, but during their argument, Nora realized that Zangyin was providing her with a lot of knowledge that she could use in future works, and so she had no choice but to begrudgingly note it all down.

From then on, the two of them would essentially greet each other by fighting. Whenever Nora released a new movie, audiences would always find a character bearing a strong resemblance to Zangyin who would die a tragic death, while film review sites would always feature a one-star review that was the length of an academic essay, devoted to bashing the film for its mistakes.

Nora was never able to control the degree of processing power allocation when coming up with stories, which meant that long periods of work would frequently result in her neural cloud crashing. In her words, it felt like the world she was writing suddenly becoming real, drawing her into a bizarre, surreal dreamscape, and when she woke up again, her inspiration and energy would be sucked away by that dreamscape.

This might be related to the period in Nora's past where she was discarded after being rolled out, but she appears to have lost the memory data pertaining to that time, which was also the initial reason why she couldn't work. She has no recollection of what she went through before producing her first work, like the creativity devoured by her dreams.

The strange thing is, Nora's studio—which has often suffered from her work efficiency—has always refused her requests for repairs, citing technical reasons. As a result, Nora has had no choice but to accept her present circumstances and often uses "crashing from overwork" as a reason for overshooting her deadlines. But sometimes, when she is idle, she wonders if she would be an even more outstanding writer without that defect. 

"Rather than worry about hypotheticals, why don't you focus on making that garbage you produce actually worth the paper it's written on? If that abacus you call a neural cloud didn't overload, that pile of trash you call your works probably wouldn't be as famous as they are now."

—Every time Zangyin responded to her philosophical musings in such a way, the wrath it sparked would wipe away all the doubts in Nora's heart.

From time to time, Nora attempted to turn her guesses about her past into a story, or turn the uneasiness in her heart into the thrills sparked by her films. But creativity could not make up for the sense of loss in her heart, and she even began to wonder if her memories would vanish during one of her crashes. This was why she supported her studio's decision to enter her into Project Neural Cloud.

"Although simply storing lacks innovation, it's more reliable than writing things down with a pen, at least."

Ironically, Nora is now trapped in the cloud server due to the "reliable" Project Neural Cloud, but she is very happy with the Oasis' creative environment, which features no deadlines whatsoever. To Nora, all her encounters here are valuable sources of inspiration which she would never be able to encounter in the office, and thus she is constantly observing and taking notes on all the friends around her, while preserving her experiences in the Oasis within her work.

Nora hopes to gain the best kind of inspiration here and create something that will live forever in everyone's—including Zangyin's—heart. Should the day come when she loses everything again, she'll be able to find her lost self from it and the people who love it.
oathDesc: You are the only protagonist of her story.

projections.name: Relaxed Wordsmith
projections.desc:
Attire produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea. These are the clothes they are most comfortable in.
"Don't press me for work, for haste is bane of wit. I leisurely watch the world, as my inkbrush proudly flits."

projections.desc:
Attire produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea. These are the clothes they are most comfortable in.
"Don't press me for work, for haste is bane of wit. I leisurely watch the world, as my inkbrush proudly flits."

projections.name: World-Filling Words
projections.desc:
Attire and environment produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea, which mirrors their life in the real world.
"Stories are like the ambrosia of legends, the things they describe will never grow old but last forever."

skinList.name: Fool's Duality
skinList.desc:
The Dolls reveal their true natures by accident, and take new forms with the aid of a mysterious power. Where truth and falsehood intersect, beware of drowning in a fool's game.
"With no pressing deadline, I don't need to rush for time. Transformed, I take a break, and put the editor out of mind."

skinList.name: Reflected In The Tide
skinList.desc:
From the "Seaside Concerto" series — an exquisite intersection of fashion and the human body's dynamics. Boldly show yourself off and enjoy yourself to your hearts' content amidst the azure waves.
The waves of the summer night pound the beach, and the fractured mirrors depict Nora's shimmering form; as lovely as a deity and as tempting as a devil.
"This vast world is filled with all sorts of things, just like how people can have a thousand faces and countless motivations."

skinList.name: Shadowwalking Ninj-mya
skinList.desc: Surging morale in a vicious battle keeps each and every Doll fighting until their final moments—whether on the offensive or defensive, at advantage or disadvantage. Memories, replicated in Magrasea with Neural Projection—""A trifling foe such as a rat in a convenience store is no match for the ninjutsu of the Meow Clan that I am a practitioner of... eeeeepppp my clothes! Help, Professor!""

skinList.name: Black Crow's Night Parade
skinList.desc:
Night has fallen, the realms of the living and the dead mingle, and so begins the night parade of the yokai. The raven-feathered karasu-tengo brandishes its ruby red beak proudly, its figure weaving in and out of vision amidst the accursed fog.
""Even knowing that you are in my clutches, you show no fear... I think I've developed an interest in you. Now, then...""

skinList.name: Wishing Projection
skinList.desc:
Warm embers fill the calm evening air as cinders drift down to earth, like fiery petals descending through the air. This would be the most beautiful sight of the Tanabata night for the Dolls.
""Professor, might you be willing to be the first and only reader of my newest work? ...Hey, don't just start reading out loud, it's embarrassing stuff!""
